package_info.package_versions: [2.205, 2.219) for Jenkins 2.205.x; ( , 2.204.2) for Jenkins LTS 2.204.x and below
package_info.why_malicious: The package is not intentionally malicious, but contains a critical vulnerability (CVE-2020-2100) that allows attackers to abuse Jenkins' UDP multicast/broadcast discovery protocol for network amplification/reflection attacks and infinite reply loops, leading to denial of service (DoS) and potential DDoS attacks against arbitrary targets.

execution_context.trigger: network request (UDP packet) received on port 33848
execution_context.file_location: jenkins-core discovery protocol implementation (Java class handling UDP multicast/broadcast)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Responds to any UDP packet received on the Jenkins discovery port (33848) with a large metadata response, regardless of the source IP or packet content.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code responds to any UDP packet, including those with spoofed source IPs, with a large response, enabling amplification/reflection attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would validate the source of discovery requests and limit responses to legitimate clients, not blindly respond to any packet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Service discovery protocols may respond to legitimate multicast/broadcast requests within a trusted network.

execution_context.trigger: network request (UDP packet) received from another Jenkins instance
execution_context.file_location: jenkins-core discovery protocol implementation (Java class handling UDP multicast/broadcast)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Responds to every UDP discovery request, even those originating from other Jenkins servers, causing two servers to enter an infinite loop of replies.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code does not discriminate between legitimate and spoofed requests, allowing two Jenkins servers to endlessly reply to each other, exhausting resources.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would include rate limiting, request validation, or loop prevention to avoid infinite reply chains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Service discovery protocols may reply to legitimate peer requests, but should prevent reply loops.

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a UDP packet with the victim's IP as the source and sends it to a vulnerable Jenkins server on port 33848.
attack_chain.leads_to: Jenkins server sends a large response to the victim, amplifying the attack traffic.

attack_chain.action: Jenkins server responds with a large metadata packet to the victim's IP, causing network amplification/reflection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim is flooded with unsolicited traffic, leading to potential denial of service.

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts UDP packets with the source and destination IPs set to two different vulnerable Jenkins servers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Both Jenkins servers enter an infinite loop, repeatedly replying to each other's discovery packets.

attack_chain.action: Infinite reply loop between Jenkins servers causes resource exhaustion and denial of service on both servers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Both Jenkins servers become unresponsive or crash.

behavioral_signatures: Large UDP responses to small requests
Frequent UDP traffic between Jenkins servers
Repeated UDP packets with similar payloads in both directions
network_indicators: Unsolicited UDP responses from Jenkins servers to external IPs
High volume of UDP traffic on port 33848
UDP packets with Jenkins metadata payloads
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Jenkins servers responding to UDP packets on port 33848, especially with large payloads to external or unexpected IP addresses. Look for patterns of repeated UDP traffic between Jenkins servers or to/from the same external IPs. Use network IDS/IPS to flag amplification patterns and infinite reply loops. Scan for vulnerable Jenkins-core versions in your environment.
